params.body:
> **Rebased and stacked.** Supersedes #349, which conflicted with `main` (after PRs 346, 352 and 354) on `docs/bedrijfsregels/90-x-bevindingen.md`. Finding renumbered **X-124 → X-130**; the three references (`MailPreview`, `MailDealerBlockTest`, `CustomAddressTest`) follow. Rules R P1-2.17, R P1-2.18 and R S4-8.13 are unchanged and still free on main. **Stacked on PR A (#357, `ui/form-controls-legible-on-phone-3`) and PR B (#358, `ui/relation-picker-3`); merge in order A, B, then this one.** Until A and B merge, GitHub shows their commits and files in this PR as well; that is expected, this branch is built on B's tip.

Shane received a confirmation mail after a buy-over with two defects in the same block: his square logo filled the whole message next to a thin column of address text, and the address read `Langestraat , 9150 Kruibeke`. Recorded as X-124.

## Where the address is composed now

`App\Http\Helpers\Custom::address($source, $prefix = '')` (the `Custom` facade, so `Custom::address($dealer)` works in every blade, controller and PDF builder). It composes from the parts that are filled in: `street street_no+addition` and `zipcode city`, joined by a comma only when both halves exist, nothing at all when nothing is filled in. It reads a model or an array, and an optional prefix covers the tables that carry the same shape (`pick_up_`, `delivery_`).

Two details that are not obvious. `street_no` and `zipcode` are `int NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so an empty house number is a `0` in the database: a zero counts as absent, because "Langestraat 0" is worse than "Langestraat". And a street with a double space (from the input) is collapsed, because that ends up on a document too.

The house number was never printed at all in four of the five mails: the column is `street_no`, the views wrote `$dealer->streetno`. That is why the separator was left hanging.

## Everywhere an address was glued by hand

Fixed, identical expression:

- `resources/views/mails/bought_email.blade.php` (`streetno`)
- `resources/views/mails/sold_email.blade.php` (`street_no`)
- `resources/views/mails/resend_export_mail.blade.php` (`streetno`)
- `resources/views/mails/export_dealer.blade.php` (`streetno`)
- `resources/views/mails/vehicle_delivered.blade.php` (`streetno`)
- `resources/views/ownstock/showroom_vehicle.blade.php` (the showroom slide, `street_no`)

Left alone, with the reason:

- `resources/views/stocklist/index_card.blade.php` and `resources/views/stocklist/_tabs/buybox.blade.php` glue the same four fields but add a distance and a `street_no_addition`, and both sit in screens other work is touching tonight.
- `resources/js/vehicle/vehicle.js:116` builds the same line in javascript for the transport form. The same rule belongs there, but it is a second language and a second place to test.
- `app/Models/Vehicle/Transport.php:76,81` compose pick-up and delivery with a name and a country around the address. `Custom::address($transport, 'pick_up_')` fits the middle of it; the rest is theirs.
- `app/Http/Controllers/Settings/DealerController.php:177` builds a geocoding query as `$data['street'] . $data['street_no'] . ',' . ...` — note the missing space between street and number. It feeds Google, not a reader, so changing it changes a lookup and not a document; worth a separate look.
- The offer, order, borderel, agreement and rental documents (about fourteen views plus `OfferController`, `OrderController`, `AfficheController`) print only `zipcode city`, without a street and without a separator, so they cannot produce a dangling comma. They would read better through the same helper, but that is a change to printed documents and belongs with whoever owns them.
- `app/Http/Resources/dealerExcelResource.php` and `merchantExcelResource.php` already guard with `filled()` and export a column, not a sentence.

## The logo

Every dealer logo in a mail now carries `width="120"` plus `style="width:120px;max-width:120px;height:auto;display:block;border:0;"`.

Both are needed. A mail client does not apply a stylesheet the way a browser does, so the constraint has to sit on the element; and Outlook renders through Word, which ignores `max-width` entirely but does honour the `width` attribute and scales the height with it. The inline `max-width` plus `height:auto` covers the clients that do read CSS and keeps the aspect ratio when the uploaded file is larger, which it almost always is. 120 px is a comfortable mark in a 600 px mail and leaves the address beside it instead of under it.

## What else is unguarded in these templates

Reported, not changed, because fixing it means rewriting the templates:

- The vehicle photo at the top of `bought_email`, `sold_email`, `vehicle_delivered`, `resend_export_mail`, `export_vehicle`, `export_daily_mail` and `test` carries no size either. The photo *is* guarded against a missing relation (the `@if(!is_null(...->primary_photo))` chain), but the four fallbacks range from a thumbnail to the full original, so a single `width` would either upscale a thumbnail or shrink nothing at all. Which derived size a mail should ask for is a decision (`VehicleImageService::urlVoor` exists for exactly that question), not a repair.
- `export_dealer` and `vehicle_delivered` guard the dealer with `optional()` on one line and dereference it bare on the next (`$vehicle->dealer->email`), so the `optional()` is decorative: if the dealer were really missing, the view would still fall over one line later.
- The vehicle blocks dereference `manufacturer`, `usage_category`, `category`, `transmission_type`, `fuel_type`, `paint_type` and `color` without a check, while `model` gets `optional()` in the same sentence. Every one of those is nullable on the vehicle sheet.

## Tests

- `tests/Unit/CustomAddressTest.php` — nine cases on the composition: complete, no house number, a zero as the not-filled-in value, the addition, no street, nothing at all, an object, a prefix, a double space.
- `tests/Feature/MailDealerBlockTest.php` — renders `mails.bought_email` (rendered, never sent, nothing read from the database) for a dealer with and without a house number and asserts no stray comma and no double space; asserts the rendered logo carries the width; and two guards over the source: no mail view reads `streetno` any more, and every dealer logo in a mail carries a width, a max-width and `height:auto`.

`stocklist:mail-preview` set both `streetno` and `street_no` on its sample dealer and left the logo empty, so neither defect could be seen in a preview. Both are corrected there.

Rules: R P1-2.17 (an address is composed), R P1-2.18 (an image in a mail carries its size), R S4-8.13 (what the buy-over mails show), finding X-130.
params.title: Mail: the dealer logo has a size and the address is composed (rebased)
